To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce RLgraph to enable flexible computation graph designs and efficient distributed execution for deep reinforcement learning algorithms.
RLgraph is a flexible library for defining and executing high-performance RL computation graphs in static graph and define by run paradigms.
RLgraph is a novel library that enables high performance and flexible implementation of RL algorithms, which we demonstrate by implementing and evaluating several state of the art algorithms in RL.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(a) a flexible, high-performance library for implementing and deploying RL algorithms, (b) a set of benchmarks for evaluating the performance of different RL algorithms on different environments, (c) a set of experiments that compare the performance of different algorithms on different environments.
the design of a flexible and efficient framework for implementing RL algorithms, which is capable of supporting both static graph and dynamic computation graphs.

the development of a general-purpose framework for RL, and the resulting implementation provides a flexible and extensible library for designing and deploying RL algorithms in a modular and efficient manner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RLgraph is a library for designing, implementing and executing high performance reinforcement learning algorithms in both static and define-by-run graph paradigms.
RLgraph is the first open-source, flexible library for designing and deploying RL computation graphs.

RLgraph is a powerful tool to implement and test reinforcement learning models, with the added advantage of being highly scalable and flexible, and is a must-have for anyone interested in reinforcement learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce a new library for designing and running deep reinforcement learning algorithms, and that we demonstrate its flexibility, performance and ease of use through several examples.

we provide a unified interface for defining and executing RL algorithms in both static graph (PyTorch, TensorFlow, MXNet) and define-by-run (JAX, NumPy) paradigms, with the flexibility to switch backends (distributed, non-distributed) and frameworks at runtime.
RLgraph is a library for defining, executing, and optimizing computation graphs in reinforcement learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a flexible, high-level API can be used to implement a wide variety of RL algorithms with minimal overhead, and that this approach enables rapid prototyping and testing of RL algorithms.
the separation of logical and physical graphs enables a flexible and modular approach to RL implementation, and can be applied to other domains such as robotics.
a unified library for defining and executing RL computation graphs can be used to achieve performance and stability gains in RL tasks.
